concerns.text: The verified OQMD raw_data loader supplies only composition/spacegroup metadata, NOT atomic coordinates or lattice parameters. Reconstructing bulk structures from formula + spacegroup is underdetermined (many distinct structures share a formula+spacegroup; lattice constants are not fixed by spacegroup alone), so the resulting GB supercells are not the OQMD structures the spec's US-1 requires ('download bulk configuration files'). The plan should either (a) cite a verified source that provides actual structures (e.g. OQMD/MP structure files with coordinates) or (b) state explicitly how lattice parameters are chosen (e.g. from volume_per_atom) and acknowledge that reconstructed structures are synthetic stand-ins, not OQMD records — currently the derivation is documented but the mismatch between dataset capability and the spec's data requirement is not resolved.

concerns.location: plan.md: Phase 4 (simulate_energy.py) — 'CPU EAM potential (NIST Fe-Cr class, file bundled in repo)'
concerns.text: The EAM potential file is a data resource with no cited source. Name the specific potential (author, year) and its canonical URL (e.g. NIST Interatomic Potentials Repository entry) so the bundled file is checksummed against a verifiable primary source, per Constitution Principle VI provenance requirements.

The plan targets '≥3 alloy systems' but the only EAM potential named is Fe-Cr class. If a single Fe-Cr potential is used, only one alloy system can be labeled; ≥3 systems requires ≥3 verified EAM potentials (or a multi-element potential). List which potentials cover which alloy systems, with sources, or the ≥3-system requirement is unmeetable with the stated resources.
